This page is the inventory and design for platform observability: golden
signals per app and Worker, privacy-preserving product analytics, the Admin
(`/admin`) Health view, and SLO burn alerts. The
[observability patterns page](/platform/architecture/system-design/observability-monitoring)
explains the concepts; this page records the sources, schema, bounds and
delivery plan.

## Inventory

### Golden signals

| Signal | Source today | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Worker request rate, errors, CPU and wall-time percentiles | Cloudflare GraphQL `workersInvocationsAdaptive`. Only the Perf Factory detector (`scripts/perf/perf-regression-cloudflare.mjs`) queries it, on demand, for five gateway mounts in `scripts/perf/perf-apps.json`. | Not retained, not shown in Admin |
| Gateway p95 TTFB and 5xx per app mount | GraphQL `httpRequestsAdaptiveGroups`, read by the same detector. | Not retained |
| Durable Object requests, errors, storage | GraphQL `durableObjectsInvocationsAdaptiveGroups` and `durableObjectsStorageGroups`. Nothing reads them. | Gap |
| Cold starts | No GraphQL field. Workers Observability events carry per-invocation detail, sampled at 5% (1% for the gateway and turbo cache). | Gap: estimated only |
| Worker logs and traces | `observability.enabled` in almost every `cloudflare.config.ts`, `wrangler*.jsonc` and `void.config.ts`, head-sampled at 0.05. `apps/ops-hub` is off. No `logpush` or `tail_consumers`. | Dashboard only |
| Analytics Engine | One bound dataset: `mastermind_store` (`apps/mastermind-store`). `packages/utils/src/app-switch-rum-ingest.ts` is wired in Meet and Mail, but no config binds `APP_SWITCH_RUM`. | Partial |
| Vercel preview analytics | Nothing reads Vercel metrics, and no app ships Speed Insights or `@vercel/analytics`. | Gap |
| Supabase (Postgres, PostgREST, Auth) | Nothing reads the Supabase metrics endpoint or Management API metrics. | Gap |
| GitHub Actions durations and queue times | `scripts/ci/ci-daily-sample.js` samples them by hand into a skill reference. `scripts/perf/perf-deploy-failures.mjs` lists failed production runs. | Not retained |
| Deploy markers | Deploy coordinator Durable Objects (`apps/deploy-coordinator`, read in Admin through `apps/admin/src/lib/infrastructure/deploy-coordinator.ts`), Worker deployment and version annotations (read by the detector), GitHub Deployments (`cloudflare-production-web` gates Supabase production). | Not correlated with signals |
| Request, cron and usage history | The Postgres log drain (`requests`, `log_events`, `cron_runs`, `usage_events`, `deployments`) behind Admin → Monitoring. It belongs to the Docker web runtime, which is inactive. | Stale |
| Cron Control runs | `CronLedger` Durable Object in `apps/cron-control`, with stop/resume operator routes. | Live, not in Admin |

### Product analytics

| Measure | Source today | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Platform DAU/WAU/MAU | `get_dau_count`, `get_wau_count`, `get_mau_count` over `auth.sessions`, shown on the Admin executive view. | Live, platform-wide only |
| DAU/WAU per app | No per-app activity record exists. | Gap |
| Meet minutes and participants | `private.meet_attendance_sessions` (join/leave intervals, 90-day retention, written by `apps/meet-realtime`). No rollup. | Gap |
| AI usage | `public.ai_credit_transactions` (feature, model, tokens, credits, `cost_usd`), `private.ai_studio_usage`, `private.usage_*` meter tables. Executive view shows credit totals. | Partial |
| Funnels | Only inventory commerce analytics. | Gap |
| Consent | Cookie banner behind the `cookie_consent_banner` flag (off). Meet AI consent schema. No analytics preference. | Gap |

Stores that hold personal data and must stay out of analytics: the log drain
`requests`/`log_events` (IP, user agent, user id, email),
`meet_attendance_sessions` (display name, user and guest ids),
`get_power_users` (user id, username) and `external_provider_costs`
(`actor_id`).

### Alerting

There are no Discord, email or Mira operational alerts. Mastermind receives
signed hub events at `/api/v1/mastermind/push-events`; the contract carries no
free text and only hub-issued item ids. The Perf Factory has no HTTP intake:
a T3 scheduled task runs the detector every 30 minutes and turns JSON
regression records into `perf:` cards on the Tasks Fleet board.

## Design

### Principles

- **Aggregate on read from the provider, persist only rollups.** Ingestion
  stores counts, sums and percentiles per service and time bucket. It never
  stores request rows, URLs, IPs, user agents or log text.
- **One scheduler.** Every collector is a Cron Control Worker processor.
  It inherits the ledger lease, generation fence, deadline and durable failure
  budget. No new Worker, cron trigger or queue.
- **Fail closed.** A source runs only when its job is listed in
  `CRON_CONTROL_ENABLED_JOBS` *and* its database control row says `on` or
  `dry_run`. A missing row, an unknown mode or a stale generation means off.
- **Source-aware reads.** Admin shows `unavailable`, `partial` and
  `suppressed` distinctly from a measured zero, following the executive view.

### Ingestion

```text
Cron Control (*/15) ── processor per source ──► provider read API (GET / GraphQL)
        │                                            │ bounded pages
        ▼                                            ▼
private.observability_source_control  ◄── fence ──  normalize to rollup rows
        │                                            │
        └──────── private RPC (service key) ─────────► upsert_observability_rollups
                                                     record_observability_ingest_run
```

| Source id | Cadence | Reads | Credential (by name) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cloudflare-workers` | 15 min | One GraphQL request for `workersInvocationsAdaptive` (ten series: the sums of requests, errors and subrequests; CPU and wall-time p50 and p99; request-duration p50, p95 and p99; quantiles arrive in microseconds and are stored as ms) and one for `durableObjectsInvocationsAdaptiveGroups` (sum of requests and errors), grouped by `scriptName` and `datetimeFifteenMinutes`. Durable Object ids, names and colos are never selected. | `CLOUDFLARE_ANALYTICS_API_TOKEN` (Account Analytics Read), account id from the Worker config |
| `cloudflare-gateway` | 15 min | `httpRequestsAdaptiveGroups` per app mount from `scripts/perf/perf-apps.json`: requests, 5xx, TTFB p50/p95/p99 | A token with Zone Analytics Read, `CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID` |
| `github-actions` | 30 min | Workflow runs of `tutur3u/platform` created in each closed 15-minute bucket: run count, failures, duration and queue time (`run_started_at - created_at`) per workflow, and successful production deploy runs on `main` as deploy markers (app, head SHA, completion time). | `GITHUB_ACTIONS_READ_TOKEN` (fine-grained, Actions read) |
| `vercel` | 30 min | Deployments per project as deploy markers. Request metrics need Observability Plus or a drain and stay out of scope until a provider decision. | `VERCEL_OBSERVABILITY_READ_TOKEN` |
| `supabase` | 15 min | Project metrics endpoint (Prometheus text): connections, CPU, disk, PostgREST and Auth request counters, parsed into the allowlisted gauges only | `SUPABASE_METRICS_READ_SECRET` |

Durable Object storage (`durableObjectsStorageGroups`) is not read yet.
Workflow deploy markers say when a deploy finished; Worker version
annotations, which the Perf Factory detector reads, remain the source for
per-version suspects.

Every token is read-only and scoped to the account or project it reads. Values
are never logged, stored or returned; logs carry the source id, counts and the
HTTP status class only.

**Bounds per run.** Each source row sets `max_requests_per_run` (default 4,
hard cap 10). Responses are capped at 1 MiB and writes at 5,000 rollup rows
and 200 deploy markers. A Cloudflare run reads at most four 15-minute
buckets starting two buckets before the watermark, so it commits at most two
new buckets per 15-minute slot and gains one bucket per slot after an outage.
Four buckets of about 100 scripts at 12 metrics are about 4,800 rows, inside
the 5,000-row write cap. A GitHub run reads up to twelve 15-minute buckets
per 30-minute slot, one request per page of 100 runs, and moves the watermark
only past buckets it read whole. When the first bucket alone needs more pages
than the run's budget, or more than the listing's 1,000 results, it is stored
as a sample (`runs` from the listing total, `sampled_runs` from what was
read) and the watermark moves on, so one busy bucket cannot stall the
source. Reads stop at seven days back; anything older stays a
recorded gap. A run that reaches a cap records `budget_exhausted` and keeps
its watermark at the last complete bucket, and the next slot continues. There is no in-run retry. The Cloudflare
GraphQL API allows 300 queries per 5 minutes; these sources issue at most 2
per 15-minute slot.

**Idempotence.** Rollup rows are keyed on
`(source, service, metric, bucket_seconds, bucket_start)` and upserted with
the newest observation, so a repeated or overlapping slot converges. Adaptive
analytics can revise recent buckets; the Cloudflare collector re-reads the
last two closed buckets each run.

**Stop fence.** Each source has its own Cron Control job, so
`/control/jobs/{id}/stop` stops exactly that source. The database adds a
second fence: `private.observability_source_control` holds one row per source
with `mode` (`off`, `dry_run`, `on`), `max_requests_per_run`, a daily row
budget and a `generation` that any mode or budget change increments. This
generation is separate from the Cron Control ledger generation. Rows start
`off`. The processor reads the row at start, checks the Cron Control fence
before every provider request and before the write, and passes the database
generation to the write RPC, which refuses a stale generation, a source that
is not `on`, and a write past the day's row budget. `dry_run` performs the
reads and records counts without writing rollups. A failed or unknown run
counts toward Cron Control's consecutive-failure budget, which stops the job
after five until an operator resumes it.

**Cost envelope.** Each source writes at most its daily row budget:
150,000 rows for `cloudflare-workers` and 40,000 for `github-actions`.
Expected volume is about 115,000 and 12,000 rows a day: about 100 scripts ×
12 metrics × 96 buckets (10 Worker metrics plus Durable Object requests and
errors), and about 20 active workflows per bucket × 6 metrics (`runs`,
`failed_runs`, duration and queue p50/p95) × 96 buckets. Both sources write
15-minute rollups, kept for 90 days (hourly rollups, which no source writes
yet, would be kept for 400 days), so the store is capped at about 17.1 M rows
((150,000 + 40,000) × 90) and expected near 11.4 M. Collectors run 144 times a day, plus 48 product analytics
and 144 retention runs: about 340 Worker invocations and under 700 PostgREST
calls a day. `prune_observability_rollups` runs in its own
`observability-retention` job, at most 1,000 rows per table every 10 minutes
(144,000 a day, above the expected daily expiry of about 127,000). GraphQL Analytics and the
GitHub read API are not billed per call.

### Schema

All tables live in `private` and have RLS enabled with no policies. Clients
have no table privileges; Cron Control reaches them only through `SECURITY
DEFINER` RPCs executable by `service_role`. Admin reads through
`/api/v1/infrastructure/` routes that check `view_infrastructure`.

| Table | Key | Holds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `observability_source_control` | `source` | Mode, request and daily row budgets, generation, watermark. |
| `observability_daily_writes` | `(source, day)` | Rows written per UTC day, for the row budget. |
| `observability_ingest_runs` | `id` | Source, window, status, request and row counts. Counts only. |
| `observability_rollups` | `(source, service, metric, bucket_seconds, bucket_start)` | Numeric value from an allowlisted metric set. |
| `observability_deploy_markers` | `(source, service, version_id)` | Deploy time, SHA, kind (`deploy`, `rollback`, `promotion`). |
| `product_analytics_daily` | `(day, app, metric, dimension)` | Aggregate value, `suppressed` flag. |
| `observability_slos` | `id` | Service, indicator, objective, window, owner role. |
| `observability_alerts` | `dedupe_key` | SLO, burn rates, state (`firing`, `resolved`), delivery receipts. |

The cost discovery work shares the scheduler, the source-control and ingest-run
tables, and the Cloudflare read client. Its billing facts (minor units,
currency, statement identities) stay in their own tables.

### Product analytics and privacy

Product analytics follows the
[data protection standard](/platform/data-protection-standard):

- **Aggregates only.** `private.rollup_product_analytics_daily(p_limit)` runs
  inside Postgres as a Cron Control maintenance RPC every 30 minutes and
  writes `(day, app, metric, dimension, value)` for the current and previous
  UTC day. Session-based counts keep the highest value seen for the day,
  because `auth.sessions` rows move forward or disappear after the day ends.
  It never copies a user, guest, workspace or meeting id, a name or free text
  into the analytics store.
- **Small cells are suppressed whole.** A cell whose cohort has 1 to 9
  people is stored as `suppressed = true` with a null value for every metric
  in it, including sums such as minutes, tokens and credits. Zero stays a
  measured zero.
- **Complements are suppressed.** AI features with fewer than 10 people are
  merged into an `other` cell. When `other` itself has 1 to 9 people, it and
  the all-feature total are both suppressed, so no small cell can be derived
  by subtraction. Per-app activity counts will follow the same rule against
  the platform totals.
- **Retention.** Daily aggregates are kept for 25 months. They are treated as
  personal data with that bounded schedule until anonymization is verified;
  they are not claimed as anonymized aggregates.
- **Inputs keep their own clocks.** The rollup reads source tables inside
  their existing retention (for example Meet attendance at 90 days) and does
  not extend it.

| Metric | Input | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dau`, `wau` (platform) | `auth.sessions` | Same definitions as the executive view. |
| `dau`, `wau` per app | `private.app_activity_marks` | Needs a new writer; see below. |
| `meet_minutes`, `meet_participants`, `meet_meetings` | `private.meet_attendance_sessions` | Minutes clipped to the day; open intervals count until the rollup time. |
| `ai_requests`, `ai_tokens`, `ai_credits`, `ai_users` per feature | `public.ai_credit_transactions` (`deduction`) | Feature names are code identifiers. |
| `signups`, `workspaces_created` | `auth.users`, `public.workspaces` | Daily counts. |

**Purpose and basis.** `product_analytics_daily` serves one purpose:
aggregate product health for platform operators with `view_infrastructure`.
The intended basis is legitimate interest. It holds no subject-level rows, so
a subject export has nothing to return from it, and an erasure does not
recompute closed days, whose counts cannot be traced to a person. The
`observability-product-analytics` job stays out of `CRON_CONTROL_ENABLED_JOBS`
until the legal owner confirms this record.

**Per-app activity.** No store records which app a person used. The planned
writer marks activity once per person, app and UTC day from the satellite
session resolver. It stores `HMAC(key(day, app), user_id)`, with one key per
day and app that lives until that UTC day closes, so marks cannot be joined
across apps or days. Runs during the day only count marks. The first run
after the day closes writes the final count, then deletes that day's marks
and key in the same transaction. Before inserting, the writer checks the
account-level usage analytics preference and pending erasure; turning the
preference off deletes that person's marks for the open day. The writer needs
the legal owner's confirmation of its basis and its own privacy review,
because a keyed hash is personal data while the key exists.

### Admin Health view

`/admin` → Monitoring → **Health** (`/monitoring/health`) shows one row per app
and Worker: request rate, error rate, p95 latency, CPU p99, DO errors, and the
latest deploy, each with a status against its SLO. Selecting a service opens a
drill-down with 15-minute series for 24 hours, 7 days or 30 days, deploy
markers drawn on every chart, and the product analytics for that app. Every
value carries its source state, and nothing outside `view_infrastructure` can
read it.

### SLOs and alerts

`private.observability_slos` names a service (a Worker script, or `*` for
every script with traffic in the last six hours), an indicator and an
objective. The defaults are `workers-availability` (99.5% of requests
without errors) and `workers-latency` (99% of requests in 15-minute buckets
whose p95 stays at or under 1,000 ms). Bucket quantiles approximate the
request-level latency indicator. The `observability-slo-burn` job runs
`private.evaluate_observability_slos` every 15 minutes, at most 500 SLO and
service pairs per pass, and evaluates multi-window burn rates (bad share
divided by the error budget):

| Severity | Long window | Short window | Burn rate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Page | 1 hour | 15 minutes (latest bucket) | 14.4 |
| Ticket | 6 hours | 1 hour | 6 |

A window with fewer than 50 requests, or with more than a quarter of its
buckets missing, is `unavailable`: it neither fires, extends nor resolves an
alert. An open alert resolves after two consecutive healthy evaluations.
Alerts are keyed by SLO, severity, service and start bucket, and resolved
alerts are kept for 90 days. Each transition (fired, resolved) is delivered
once, at most 20 per pass:

- **Owner notification** through the shared
  `private.send_root_operator_alert` RPC (shared with cost alerts), which
  dedupes per key and calls `public.create_notification` for root workspace
  members holding `view_infrastructure`. This reaches the web inbox, email
  and push, honoring each person's notification preferences; page burns are
  `urgent`. A delivery that creates no notification is retried on the next
  pass. Mira sees the same notification; there is no separate Mira channel.
- **Admin** through `GET /api/v1/infrastructure/observability/alerts`,
  which returns firing and recently resolved alerts to a root member with
  `view_infrastructure` (session or bearer token). The alert type and parser
  are shared from `@tuturuuu/utils/observability/alerts`.
- **Mastermind fleet sync** (see
  [Fleet sync](/platform/features/mobile-mastermind#fleet-sync)): Web reads
  firing alerts with their SLO indicator server-side with the admin client
  (filtered, ordered and limited in the query), memoized per isolate for
  60 seconds (15 seconds after a failure), and serves firing alerts only
  (at most 20, pages first, then newest) to the owner's phone on
  `GET /api/v1/mastermind/fleet/state` and to the orchestrator Mac on the
  HMAC-signed `GET /api/v1/mastermind/fleet/alerts`. The Mac never holds an
  infrastructure token. The orchestrator relays each new page burn to the
  owner's ask channel once per alert id; tickets and resolved alerts raise
  no ask. The push-event contract stays unchanged.
- **Perf Factory** through the same route's `regressions`: firing alerts in
  the detector's record shape (`id`, `app`, `worker`, `metric`, `startTime`,
  `detectedAt`, `baseline`, `trigger`, `observed`, `windows`,
  `baselineWindows`, `rule`, `suspects`, `versionSummary`, `queries`) with
  `source: "observability-slo"`. `scripts/perf/perf-observability-alerts.mjs`
  writes them for the dispatcher, which fills `suspects` and `versionSummary`
  from Worker version annotations with the detector's `rerun` before intake.

## Delivery plan

| Slice | Scope | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| (a) | This inventory and design. | Docs review |
| (b) | Schema, source control, `cloudflare-workers` (Workers and Durable Objects), and `github-actions` collectors, product analytics rollup, retention. Jobs and rows start off. | Processor tests for bounds, fence, idempotence, dry run and failure budget; pgTAP for grants and the generation check |
| (c) | Admin Health page and drill-down, en and vi. | Component and route tests, 390 px and 1440 px renders |
| (d) | SLO table, burn evaluator, notification, Mastermind and Perf Factory delivery. | Burn-rate fixtures, delivery receipts, detector intake test |

The `cloudflare-gateway`, Vercel and Supabase collectors and the per-app
activity writer follow once their tokens are provisioned and their reviews
pass. The Perf Factory detector covers gateway mounts until then.

## Operating

- Enable a source: provision its token, set its control row to `dry_run`,
  add the job to `CRON_CONTROL_ENABLED_JOBS`, check the run log, then set `on`.
- Stop a source now: stop its job with `/control/jobs/{id}/stop`. The
  collector checks that fence before every provider request and before the
  write. Setting the control row to `off` also stops it: a running collector
  finishes its in-flight read, and the write is refused.
- Investigate a missing series: read `observability_ingest_runs` for the source
  (`budget_exhausted`, `failed`, `unknown`) before reading provider dashboards.
